## Introduction

The **Gamma distribution** is a two-parameter family of continuous
probability distributions that generalises the
[[exponential-distribution]]. It arises naturally as the sum of
independent exponential random variables and is used to model waiting
times, lifetimes, and rates.

:::{.definition data-title="Gamma Distribution"}

A random variable $X$ follows a **Gamma distribution** with shape
parameter $\alpha > 0$ and rate parameter $\beta > 0$ if

$$
X \sim \text{Gamma}(\alpha, \beta) \quad \text{or}
  \quad X \sim \Gamma(\alpha, \beta).
$$

:::

*Parameterisations:* The **shape-rate** form uses $\alpha$ (shape) and
$\beta$ (rate); the **shape-scale** form uses $\alpha$ and
$\theta = 1/\beta$ (scale). We use shape-rate here.

## Probability Density Function

:::{.definition data-title="Probability Density Function (PDF)"}

The probability density function (shape-rate form) is

$$
f(x) = \frac{\beta^\alpha}{\Gamma(\alpha)} x^{\alpha - 1}
  e^{-\beta x}, \quad x > 0,
$$

where $\Gamma(\alpha)$ is the gamma function.

:::

*Interpretation:* The shape $\alpha$ controls how peaked the density is
and the rate $\beta$ sets the scale; for $\alpha \leq 1$ the density is
strictly decreasing, and for $\alpha > 1$ it is unimodal.

::: {#7a5007a4 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Plotting code"}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import gamma

sns.set_style('whitegrid')
sns.set_palette('Set2')

x = np.linspace(0, 20, 400)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
for a in (1, 2, 5, 9):
    ax.plot(x, gamma.pdf(x, a, scale=1),
            lw=2, label=rf'$\alpha = {a}$')

ax.set_xlabel('$x$')
ax.set_ylabel('$f(x)$')
ax.set_title(r'Gamma density ($\beta = 1$)')
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

## Key Properties

:::{.theorem data-title="Moments of the Gamma Distribution"}

The expectation and variance of $X \sim \text{Gamma}(\alpha, \beta)$ are

$$
\mathbb{E}[X] = \frac{\alpha}{\beta} \quad \& \quad
  \operatorname{Var}(X) = \frac{\alpha}{\beta^2}.
$$

:::

:::{.proof}

Using $\int_0^\infty x^{\alpha} e^{-\beta x} \, dx =
\Gamma(\alpha + 1)/\beta^{\alpha + 1}$,

$$
\mathbb{E}[X] = \frac{\beta^\alpha}{\Gamma(\alpha)}
  \cdot \frac{\Gamma(\alpha + 1)}{\beta^{\alpha + 1}}
  = \frac{\alpha}{\beta}.
$$

Similarly $\mathbb{E}[X^2] = \alpha(\alpha + 1)/\beta^2$, so
$\operatorname{Var}(X) = \alpha/\beta^2$.

:::

## Generating Functions

:::{.theorem data-title="Moment Generating Function"}

The **moment generating function (MGF)** of
$X \sim \text{Gamma}(\alpha, \beta)$ is

$$
M_X(t) = \left(\frac{\beta}{\beta - t}\right)^\alpha,
  \quad t < \beta.
$$

:::

:::{.theorem data-title="Characteristic Function"}

The characteristic function of $X \sim \text{Gamma}(\alpha, \beta)$ is

$$
\varphi_X(t) = \left(\frac{\beta}{\beta - it}\right)^\alpha.
$$

:::

## Sums of Independent Gamma RVs

:::{.theorem data-title="Additivity of the Gamma Distribution"}

If $X_i \sim \text{Gamma}(\alpha_i, \beta)$ are independent (same rate
$\beta$), then

$$
\sum_{i=1}^n X_i \sim
  \text{Gamma}\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n \alpha_i, \beta\right).
$$

:::

:::{.proof}

The MGF product gives
$\prod_{i=1}^n (\beta/(\beta - t))^{\alpha_i}
= (\beta/(\beta - t))^{\sum_i \alpha_i}$.

:::

In particular, if $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ are i.i.d.
$\text{Exponential}(\beta)$, then
$X_1 + \cdots + X_n \sim \text{Gamma}(n, \beta)$, so the Gamma
distribution models the total of $n$ independent waiting times.

## Special Cases and Relationships

- **[[exponential-distribution]]:** $\text{Gamma}(1, \beta) =
  \text{Exponential}(\beta)$.
- **Erlang:** When $\alpha = n$ is a positive integer,
  $\text{Gamma}(n, \beta)$ is the Erlang distribution.
- **[[chi-squared-distribution]]:** $\text{Gamma}(k/2, 1/2) = \chi^2_k$.
- **[[beta-distribution]]:** If $U \sim \text{Gamma}(\alpha, 1)$ and
  $V \sim \text{Gamma}(\beta, 1)$ are independent, then
  $\frac{U}{U + V} \sim \text{Beta}(\alpha, \beta)$.

## Examples and Applications

:::{.example data-title="Waiting for many events"}

The total time to wait for $n$ events in a Poisson process — the sum of
$n$ exponential inter-arrival times — is $\text{Gamma}(n, \lambda)$.

:::

:::{.example data-title="Reliability"}

The lifetime of a system with parallel redundant components can be
modelled with a Gamma distribution.

:::

:::{.example data-title="Bayesian priors"}

The Gamma distribution is the conjugate prior for the rate parameter of a
Poisson or exponential likelihood.

:::
